<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XXV.|ACCORDING TO S. MATTHEW.|71 HOLY weeke.}}</noinclude>''12. Iniquity abound.''] When Heresie and false teachers reigne in the world, namely toward the later day, wicked life aboundeth, and charity decayeth.

''14. Shal be preached.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel now preached to Infidels.}}The Gospel hath been preached of late yeres, and now is, by holy Religious men of diuers Orders, in sundry great Countries which neuer heard the Gospel before, as it is thought.

''15. Abomination of desolation.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The abomination of desolation.}}This abomination of desolation foretold, was first partly fulfilled in diuerse prophanations of the Temple of Hierusalem, when the sacrifice and seruice of God was taken away. but specially it shal be fulfilled by Antichrist and his Precursors, when they shal abolishe the holy Masse, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The abolishing of the holy sacrifice of the Masse by Antichrist and his ministers.}}which is the Sacrifice of Christes body and bloud, and the only soueraine worship dewe to God in his Church: as S. Hyppolytus writeth in these wordes: The Churches shal lament with great lamentation, because there shal neither oblation be made, nor incense, nor worship grateful to God. But the sacred houses of Churches shal be like to cottages, and the pretious body and bloud of Christ shal not be extant (openly in Churches) in those dayes, the Liturgie (or Masse) shal be extinguished, the Psalmodie shal cease, the reciting of the Scriptures shal not be heard. ''Hippol. de Antichristo''. By which it is plaine that the Heretikes of these daies be the special fore-runners of Antichrist.

''22. Shal be shortened.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Antichrist.}}The reigne of Antichrist shal be short, that is, three yeres and a halfe. ''Dan. 7. Apoc. 11''. Therfore the Heretikes are blasphemous and ridiculous, that say, Christes Vicar is Antichrist, who hath sitten these 1500 yeres.

''24. Great signes.''] These signes and miracles shal be to the outward appearance only, for S. Paule calleth them {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''2. Thes. 2.''}}* lying signes, to seduce them only that shal perish. Wherby we see that if Heretikes could worke feyned and forged miracles, yet we ought not to beleeue them, much lesse when they can not so much as seeme to doe any.

''26. In closets.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The secrete cōuenticles of Heretikes.}}Christ hauing made the Churches authority bright and clere to the whole world, warneth the faithful to take heede of Heretikes and Schismatikes, which haue their conuenticles aside in certaine odde places and obscure corners, alluring curious persons vnto them. ''Aug. li. 1. q. Euang. q. 38''. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Catholike Christians secretely assembling in time of persecution.}}For as for the comming together of Catholikes to serue God in secrete places, that is a necessarie thing in time of persecution, and was vsed of Christians for three hundred yeres together after Christ, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 1, 12.''}}* and the Apostles also and disciples came so together in Hierusalem for feare of the Iewes. And Catholikes doe the same at this day in our countrie, not drawing religion into corners from the society of the Catholike Church, but practising secretely the same faith, that in al Christendom shineth and appeareth most gloriously.

''29. Immediatly.''] {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=Antichrist.}}If the later day shal immediatly folow the persecution of Antichrist, which is to endure but three yeres and a halfe, as is aforesaid: then is it mere blasphemie to say, Gods Vicar is Antichrist, and that (by their owne limitation) these thousand yeres almost.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XXV.}}}}}}

{{c|''Continuing his Sermon, he bringeth two parables, of ten Virgins, and of Talents, to shew how it shalbe in Domesday with the Faithful that prepare, and that prepare not them selues. 31. Then also without parables he sheweth that such Faithful as doe workes of mercy, shal haue for them life euerlasting: and such as doe not, euerlasting damnation.''}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel for holy Virgins.}}{{dropinitial|T|fl={{verse|chapter=25|verse=1}}}}{{sc|Hen}} shal the kingdom of heauen be like to ten {{sup|‖}} virgins: which taking their {{sup|‖}} lampes vvent forth to meete the bridegrome and the bride. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=2}}† And fiue of them were foolish, and fiue vvise. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=3}}† but the fiue foolish, hauing taken their lampes, did not take {{sup|‖}} oile vvith them: {{verse|chapter=25|verse=4}}† but the vvise did take oile in their vessels vvith the lampes. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=5}}† And the bridegrome tarying long, they slumbered all and slept. {{verse|chapter=25|verse=6}}† And at midnight there vvas a clamour made, Behold the bridegrome commeth, goe<noinclude>{{rh|||ye}}</noinclude>
